scope: review of the round 2 fixes (diffs 469c835..HEAD on tincan-core/tincan-net, a0cb57e..HEAD on tincan-files, tincan-app, src-tauri, ui)

confirmed.problem: The admission budget (the DOS-10 fix) does not limit how many members can be created. budget_admits only charges MemberAdmit events whose author is the sender of the Events frame. Admissions written by someone else and relayed are passed through with no charge (`if ev.author != sender { out.push(s); continue; }`). On top of that, each new member gets its own fresh admit_by budget, because every member may author MemberAdmit with any known invite (state.rs:643). So per-member budgets multiply with each new identity. Members do not budget what the host fans out, so every replica accepts the result.
confirmed.scenario: Mallory, a member, publishes one MemberAdmit for a key S1 she controls; this is charged once. Offline, S1 signs a contiguous chain of 70 000 MemberAdmit events for fresh keys, using any unexpired invite (an InviteCreate by S1 works too). Each new key then signs one Profile event. Mallory sends all of this to the honest host as Ctl::Events frames on her own member link. Because the author is S1, not Mallory, nothing is charged or held back. The host stores and fans out every event, so every replica grows permanently. Once there are more than 65 536 authors with events, honest heads need more than HeadsAssembler::MAX_ENTRIES (wire.rs:513) entries. Every receiver then clears the SyncHavePart assembly, no SyncHave is ever handled, and history sync stops for everyone. That is DOS-10 again. Fewer sybils (20 instantly through her own budget, any number this way) also feed NET-SECURITY-2.
confirmed.fix: (1) Budget every admission of someone who is not yet a member, on every path: JoinRequest, Publish, own and relayed Events, probe and retired-probe links. Charge it to a root responsible member, not the author. Walk up the chain of admitters (the MemberAdmit author, or the invite's creator for joins) to the nearest ancestor whose admission this replica stored before this host role started. Use local time, not hlc. A freshly admitted sybil then spends its admitter's bucket and never gets a fresh one. (2) Add a host-wide backstop bucket for new-member admissions. When it is over budget, hold back that author's remaining events in the batch and set resync_at; never drop them. (3) On the member side, bound new-member admissions accepted per host link per time window in the same way: hold them back and re-request with a later SyncHave, so a malicious host cannot flood either. (4) Make the heads cliff non-fatal. After an overflow, HeadsAssembler must discard every part up to and including the next more=false instead of returning a truncated Heads. A member whose heads could not be assembled must not be left unable to publish forever. Tests: in tests_security, a member relays 200 admissions signed by an admitted sybil and the host applies at most the budget; sybils that each admit 20 do not multiply the total; in wire, a unit test that an overflowed assembly yields None for the whole sequence.
confirmed.verify:
Confirmed on main afc192c, which is what the issue's line numbers match; dm.rs changed a lot since a0cb57e. budget_admits (host.rs:841-844) passes every event not authored by the sender with no charge. state.rs:643-647 lets any member author MemberAdmit with any known, unexpired invite. member.rs:171-173 ingests host fan-out with no budget. So: Mallory makes one charged admit of S1. She then relays S1's chain of admissions and each sybil's Profile on her own member link. The host applies, stores and fans all of it out (host.rs:1206-1217).

Own-authored admissions also multiply without relaying. admit_by is keyed per identity (host.rs:234, 859), so each admitted sybil that connects gets a fresh burst of 20 (20 -> 400 -> 8000).

The architecture.md residual-risk text admits the relay bypass, but only as a merge concern. It never mentions this consequence, which is worse than the issue says. With 65,537 to 73,728 authors, HeadsAssembler::push (wire.rs:516-520) clears the assembly and the last part returns None. Every member's post-Welcome SyncHavePart therefore never assembles at the host (host.rs:1228-1231), so request_sync never runs. The empty last page never arrives, m.synced stays false, and pump_publishes (mod.rs:1197) blocks the member's publishes forever: every queued publish fails with NotConnected after 15 s. Every member that reconnects is left read-only. Above that band, push returns a truncated Heads after the clear, so every resync re-sends nearly the whole history.

The damage is permanent (events cannot be removed) and takes one insider a few minutes. Also, the host-side fix alone is not enough. A malicious member can legitimately become host (online first, or NET-SECURITY-2) and fan the same flood out directly, and members budget nothing they receive from the host.

confirmed.problem: The S1 fix (attested merge) can still be beaten with sybil members. verified_for counts any attestation for the peer's claim if it is fresh, validly signed, from a current member, and from someone not connected to me. Sybil members fit all of these: a member admits them through its own budget (20 at once) or for free through NET-SECURITY-1. Their keys can sign attestations without ever connecting to anyone. may_yield(links, theirs_verified) and may_follow then hand all honest members to the attacker.
confirmed.scenario: Alice hosts with 10 attested members, Mallory among them. Mallory publishes 20 MemberAdmit events for her own keys, each accepted within her burst of 20. Each sybil signs Attestation{server, host: Mallory, epoch: E+1}. Mallory sends HostCompare2{claim(Mallory, E+1), attests: 20 sybil attestations} on her member link. Alice counts theirs_verified = 20 against 9 of her own (Mallory excluded). merge_winner_attested picks Mallory, and may_yield(9, 20) is true. Mallory sends HostMoved{epoch E+2}. may_follow passes, and Alice relays the HostMoved and redirects all 9 honest members to Mallory. Mallory now hosts everyone. She can silently receive every voice room's audio and screen shares through the SFU, and park or refuse publishes. The same works when Alice's periodic probe dials Mallory and Mallory answers with a Welcome. MAX_ATTESTS = 64, so with NET-SECURITY-1 this defeats any host with fewer than 64 online attested members.
confirmed.fix: Count an attester only if this replica first stored its admission at least 24 h ago, by local time. Persist the first-stored time per member in kv; members already present when this ships count as old. Also exclude attesters whose admission chain leads back to the comparing peer: walk the MemberAdmit author and the invite's creator, transitively, over the last 24 h. Apply both in compare_from_member and probe_compare, and keep the may_follow re-check. Update the residual-risk text to say what is left: pre-aged sybils, and joins through a shared invite. Test: like s1_member_cannot_take_over_a_live_host, but Mallory first publishes 20 MemberAdmit for fresh keys and sends HostCompare2 with their attestations. Alice keeps hosting and her members stay.
confirmed.verify:
The mechanism holds end to end. verified_for (host.rs:531-536) counts any fresh, validly signed attestation from a current member that is not connected to me. Sybils admitted through Mallory's own Publish budget (host.rs:1379, a burst of 20) qualify and never need to connect. merge_winner_attested (election.rs:183-186) breaks ties by epoch, so Mallory needs only as many sybils as the host has other attested members, not more. may_yield and may_follow (election.rs:195, host.rs:517-520) then pass. lose_merge_links (host.rs:1069-1081) redirects every member, and member host_moved (member.rs:352-380) follows. The probe path (probe_compare, host.rs:1564-1606) is the same. This violates must-not #1 for practically every server, since few have more than 20 members online.

However, architecture.md 'Residual risks' (Sybils) documents exactly this as accepted. It rejected attester-age gating only because hlc can be backdated. The proposed local first-stored time answers that objection, but it is a mitigation, not a fix. A member can pre-provision about 64 sybils (20 at once, then one a minute) and let them age 24 h. And the 'admitted by the peer' exclusion is bypassed when sybils join with JoinRequest through a publicly shared invite of another member: the honest host then authors their MemberAdmit.

confirmed.problem: Ctl::Events from a member link bypasses the publish budget (5/s, burst 20), which is applied only to Ctl::Publish. Any new, contiguous, validly signed events in an Events frame are applied, stored and fanned out with no rate limit. Only MemberAdmit is budgeted. Fan-out pages (up to 256 KiB each) go through broadcast() as non-droppable session frames. Members whose 1024-frame live queue fills are closed as 'too slow'. This reopens N2/DOS-03 and allows unbounded storage spam on every replica.
confirmed.scenario: Mallory streams her own Message events (seq head+1, head+2, ...) inside 1 MiB Ctl::Events frames, about 3000 events per frame, as fast as her uplink allows. The host verifies, stores and fans out each frame as about 4 pages to every member. Up to 1024 pages × 256 KiB of shared Bytes (about 256 MiB) can be buffered for a slow member before broadcast() closes it as 'too slow'. It reconnects, resyncs the flood, and is dropped again. Every replica stores millions of messages, and the UI of every member is flooded. Publish's 5/s limit never applies.
confirmed.fix: In budget_admits, or a sibling budget_events used on member links and on probe and retired-probe links, charge every new (not yet stored) event applied from Events. Own events go against a per-sender bucket with a large burst (about 2000 events or 8 MiB) refilled at the publish rate. Relayed events go against a per-sender byte bucket. Over budget, hold back that author's later events in the batch (keeping contiguity), set resync_at, and resend heads later, never drop. Test: a member pushes 10 000 of its own messages through Events. The host applies at most the burst at once, the rest arrive later, and no honest member is closed as 'too slow'. A malicious host can still flood members, because members budget nothing from the host; track that as a separate member-side item.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. budget_admits (host.rs:848-863) charges only a new MemberAdmit. A sender's own Message at the next seq is pushed with no charge, and the Publish bucket (host.rs:1186) is never consulted on the Events path. Ctl::within_limits (wire.rs:463-480) puts no bound on Events, so up to MAX_FRAME, 1 MiB per frame. Applied events are fanned out as non-droppable pages (host.rs:301, 437-441). broadcast closes any member whose 1024-frame live queue is full as 'too slow' (host.rs:430-432, link.rs:32, 282). That is the N2/DOS-03 amplification again, plus unbounded storage on every replica. Relaying a sybil's messages bypasses it as well, so the budget has to apply per sender for relayed events too: charging the author is multiplied by sybils. Honest members publish one event at a time through Publish (mod.rs:1194-1227). Own new events arrive in Events only after this member hosted a separate partition, so a generous burst does not hurt them.

confirmed.problem: The pre-auth gate's known pool refuses new known peers when it is full; only the unknown pool evicts its oldest waiter. Eight known identities × MAX_PREAUTH_PER_PEER (8) = 64 fill MAX_PREAUTH. 'Known' includes every DM contact, and a stranger becomes a contact as soon as one valid first message opens a conversation (is_known_peer checks for a DM replica). After that, every incoming connection from a real member or contact gets enter_peer() == None and is closed with 'no hello'.
confirmed.scenario: An outsider who knows my user code makes 8 keys and sends one DM from each (the stranger rate allows 10 per minute). All 8 are now known. Each opens 8 QUIC connections to me and never sends a first frame, holding 64 known slots for FIRST_FRAME_TIMEOUT (4 s), then reconnects, which is about 16 connections per second. Meanwhile every member reconnecting to a server I host (after a network blip, a failover to me, a handoff, or a cold open) is refused, as is every DM contact dialing me. The servers I host stay split or hostless for as long as this goes on. A malicious server member can do the same with 7 sybils.
confirmed.fix: When the known pool is full, evict a waiter instead of refusing: the oldest waiter of the peer holding the most slots (fall back to the oldest overall), using the same Notify eviction as the unknown pool. Honest first frames arrive within one RTT, so this hurts only idle holders. Count stranger-opened DM conversations I never answered (my head == 0 and no shared server) as unknown for pre-auth. Do not lower the per-peer cap to 2 or 3: the cap of 8 exists for a peer that shares several servers and dials them all at cold open (proto.rs:26-28). Eviction by most slots already covers it. Unit test in proto.rs: 8 peers hold 8 known slots each, a new known peer still gets a slot, and one of the flooders' slots is told to give up.
confirmed.verify:
Confirmed. In enter_peer (proto.rs:84-89) the known pool returns None at MAX_PREAUTH (64); only the unknown pool evicts. is_known_peer (inner.rs:329-334) treats any DM replica as known. A stranger gets one with a single valid first message (dm.rs:968-983), and up to 32 unanswered stranger conversations are allowed. With MAX_PREAUTH_PER_PEER = 8, eight identities fill all 64 known slots for FIRST_FRAME_TIMEOUT (4 s). Every member or contact connection is then closed with 'no hello' (proto.rs:190-192, 234-236). A server member with 7 sybils can do the same. This breaks the stated guarantee that members and contacts have their own slots.

The impact is inbound only: my own outgoing dials still work, and a server I host recovers through the merge once its members elect a successor, though I lose hosting. While the attack lasts, contacts cannot reach me, DM or call me. The attacker has to keep it up at about 16 connections per second.

confirmed.problem: accept_incoming adds a stranger to dm.strangers (admit_stranger) before writing its DmHello reply. If write_ctl fails, it returns without removing the entry. Nothing else removes it, because unregister only runs for registered links. write_ctl is also a bare write_all with no timeout. A peer that grants no stream credit parks the task forever, holding the slot and the connection.
confirmed.scenario: A stranger sends a valid DmHello and immediately closes the connection, or sends STOP_SENDING on the control stream. My write_all returns ConnectionLost or Stopped, and the function returns with the stranger still in `strangers`. After 8 such connections from 8 throwaway keys, MAX_STRANGER_LINKS is reached for good. Every later stranger, including a real new contact who pasted my user code, is closed with 'busy' until I restart Tincan. With zero stream credit, the same happens without closing anything.
confirmed.fix: Hold the stranger slot in an RAII guard that removes the peer from dm.strangers on drop. Release the guard to the link only after register() kept it. From then on unregister, or stranger_frame when it opens the conversation, removes the peer as now. Wrap the hello write in tokio::time::timeout(net.timings.dial) on both the stranger and the known path, and close the connection on timeout. Test in tests_dm: 10 strangers each send DmHello and immediately stop or close. A fresh stranger can then still connect and open a conversation.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. accept_incoming calls admit_stranger, which inserts the peer into dm.strangers (dm.rs:646-656), before write_ctl (dm.rs:818-821). On Err it returns without removing the entry. Only unregister (dm.rs:617, and only for a registered link) and stranger_frame (dm.rs:980) remove it. write_ctl is a bare write_all (link.rs:105-108). A dialer that sends DmHello and then STOP_SENDING or closes makes it fail deterministically, and one that grants no stream credit parks the task with no timeout. Eight throwaway keys use up MAX_STRANGER_LINKS for good; the stranger rate allows 10 a minute, so that takes under a minute. Every later stranger gets 'busy' until restart. The documented residual risk assumes a sustained attack; this one costs nothing once done and lasts until restart.

confirmed.problem: Part of the N1 fix: a member now publishes only after the host's whole history sync to it has finished (m.synced, set by the empty last page). Queued publishes still expire after publish_timeout (15 s) in every role, including a connected member that is still syncing. When the host's sync takes longer than 15 s, messages are failed with NotConnected even though the device is connected. This can happen after a long absence, over a relay, while the host's per-member sync budget (3, then one per 10 s) delays the start, or while NET-SECURITY-9 stretches the sync over extra rounds.
confirmed.scenario: Bea comes back after two weeks to a busy server: about 25 MB of history, reached over an n0 relay at about 1 MB/s. She connects (Welcome) and types a message right away. The host's send_missing takes about 25 s. pump_publishes returns early because !m.synced, and after 15 s publish_timers answers Err(NetError::NotConnected). The UI reports 'not connected' for a connected server. Before this change, publishing only waited for her own small sync to the host (sync_out_done).
confirmed.fix: Record the host's advertised head for my own author from the SyncHave or SyncHavePart it sends right after Welcome. Allow publishing once sync_out_done holds and either m.synced is set or that head is <= my applied head for myself. Alternatively, do not let queued items expire while in Role::Member and !m.synced (with an overall cap such as 2 min). Test: a large history over a throttled sync, and a publish right after Welcome succeeds before the sync ends.
confirmed.verify:
Confirmed. A queued publish's deadline is set when it is queued, now + publish_timeout of 15 s (mod.rs:563). The member branch of pump_publishes returns early until m.synced (mod.rs:1197). publish_timers fails expired queued items with NotConnected in every role (mod.rs:1143-1153). m.synced is set only by the host's empty last page (member.rs:171-189). That page can take more than 15 s: a new joiner syncing a large server over a relay, or a start delayed by the per-member sync budget of 3, then one per 10 s, after flapping reconnects (host.rs:44-45, 679-686).

Nothing is lost: the body was never signed, and the app keeps the text. But the user sees 'not connected' for a connected server and has to resend, typically the joiner's first 'hi'. Waiting for synced is defensive anyway: the persisted own-seq floor (replica.rs:203-214) already prevents seq reuse.

confirmed.problem: Events received on a DM link have no rate or volume limit. on_frame ingests every valid event of every page with ingest_many and stores it. The per-contact gates cover only typing, rings, call state and names. A stranger is admitted as soon as its first in-order message is valid, and the rest of that frame and every later frame is stored without limit.
confirmed.scenario: An outsider with my user code opens a stranger DM connection. In one 1 MiB Ctl::Events frame they send seq 1..3000 messages, then keep sending contiguous messages of 4000 characters at link speed. stranger_opens accepts the first one. Everything is then applied and stored in my SQLite and emitted as EventAdded, gigabytes per hour, filling my disk and the DM list. The 32-unanswered-conversations cap does not help, because one conversation is enough. A real contact can do the same.
confirmed.fix: Add a per-contact bucket on applied DM events in on_frame: a small cap (about 50) while I have not written in the conversation, including the frame that opens it, and after that a burst of about 2000 refilled at a few per second. Over budget, stop applying the rest of the page and ack only what was applied. An honest sender's send_missing runs once per ack, and nothing re-sends until it reconnects. So when the bucket refills and something was cut off, send SyncHave{heads} once (rate-limited) to pull the rest. Test in tests_dm: a stranger sends 5000 messages and at most the cap is stored; a contact's backlog over the burst still arrives in full once the bucket refills.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. on_frame (dm.rs:993-1010) verifies and ingests every event of every page and acks with SyncHave. DmGates (dm.rs:99-119, 658-668) budget only typing, rings, call state and names. PendingLimits::dm bounds only early events; events that apply in order are unbounded. After stranger_opens accepts the first event (dm.rs:687-699), the same frame is passed on to on_frame (dm.rs:911-923), so the whole first frame, and every later one, is stored. Events have no within_limits bound, so up to 1 MiB per frame. One stranger conversation, or any contact, can fill my disk and flood my DM list at link speed.

confirmed.problem: First contact can be locked out permanently without NET-SECURITY-5 too. (a) Every frame from a stranger resets the 120 s idle timer before the stranger check, Ticks and DmProfile included. A stranger that never sends a message can keep one of the 8 MAX_STRANGER_LINKS slots forever, and admit_stranger refuses newcomers instead of evicting. (b) stranger_frame refuses new conversations once 32 unanswered stranger conversations exist (line 974). Nothing evicts them, and there is no API to delete a DM, so the only way out is to reply to the spam.
confirmed.scenario: (a) 8 keys each open a DM connection and send Ctl::Tick every 60 s. All 8 slots stay taken, and every real newcomer is closed with 'busy' indefinitely. (b) 32 keys each send one valid message. From then on, any new person who pastes my user code and writes to me is silently ignored ('too many unanswered stranger conversations') until I answer 32 spam threads.
confirmed.fix: (a) For a link with no conversation, do not let Tick or DmProfile extend the idle deadline. Close it if no conversation opens within about 30 s. When MAX_STRANGER_LINKS is full, evict the oldest stranger link instead of refusing. (b) Do not count unanswered stranger conversations older than a few days toward the cap, and do not auto-delete stored conversations. Add a DM delete or block API so the user can clear spam, and count only conversations the peer opened. Tests: 8 idle strangers sending Ticks do not keep a new stranger out; with 32 stale unanswered conversations, a new stranger can still open one.
confirmed.verify: (a) Confirmed: idle_at is reset for every frame before the stranger check (dm.rs:902-917), so Tick or DmProfile keeps a link with no conversation alive forever, and admit_stranger refuses newcomers instead of evicting (dm.rs:651). This is the residual risk architecture.md already accepts ('Eight stranger identities can hold every stranger DM slot...'). (b) Confirmed: stranger_frame refuses a new conversation at 32 unanswered (dm.rs:974), and nothing removes old ones. There is no DM delete or block API: Net::leave needs a server session and returns UnknownConv for DMs (net.rs:370-372). The notes document the cap. The workaround is to reply to the spam. unanswered_stranger_convs (dm.rs:672-683) also counts DMs I opened myself with dm_open or dm_watch and never wrote in. Caveat for (a)'s fix: a legitimate watcher with no conversation yet keeps its link alive with Ticks by design (notes-tincan-net.md, dm_watch). Closing such links after 30 s would make watchers reconnect over and over on the stranger rate.

confirmed.problem: PendingLimits::network() caps each author at 2048 buffered events and 4096 seqs ahead. send_missing streams one author's whole range before the next (owner first). An honest owner chain often blocks on a reference to a later author: a Delete of a newer member's message, or a MemberAdmit that uses a newer member's invite. Everything after that point in the owner's chain becomes Gap, and beyond 2048 events it is silently dropped. Members admitted in the dropped part then count as non-members, capped at 256 events in total. The empty last page still arrives, so member.rs:181 emits SyncComplete, sends Status{synced: true} (making the member eligible for succession) and unlocks publishing, while much of the history is missing until the next VvDigest round (up to 60 s, a second full sync).
confirmed.scenario: Owner Alice hosts an active server. Early on she deletes a message by Dan, who joined after her, and she later writes 6000 messages and admits 30 people. A new joiner receives Alice's chain first. Her Delete waits for Dan's message, and her next 2048 events are buffered while the other ~3950 and the later admissions are dropped. Dan's chain arrives and unblocks her, and the last page fires SyncComplete. The app ends its bulk window and marks the server synced. About 60 s later the VvDigest resync delivers the missing ~4000 events as 'live' EventAdded, and the joiner was meanwhile reported synced and eligible as a successor.
confirmed.fix: Have PendingBuffer::ingest count events it drops under the limits (expose dropped_since_mark()). On the empty last page, if anything was dropped (or is still pending for authors that are now members), send a fresh SyncHave at once and set synced and emit SyncComplete only after a later last page with nothing dropped, with a limit of about 3 rounds. To make blocking rare, have send_missing merge authors by hlc instead of streaming one author at a time. Test in tests_store: an owner chain blocked on a later member's invite, with more than 2048 owner events after it. SyncComplete comes only once every event is applied.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. send_missing streams each author's whole range in sync_author_order, owner first (replica.rs:244-302, state.rs:416-424). A host or owner chain blocks at any MemberAdmit that uses a later member's invite: missing invite -> Gap (state.rs:643-646). That is common, since any join through a non-owner invite while the owner hosted does it, and an owner's Delete of a newer member's message blocks the same way. PendingBuffer then drops events beyond 2048 per author or 4096 seqs ahead (state.rs:968-974), and members admitted in the dropped part fall under the 256 non-member cap. The empty last page still sets synced, sends Status{synced: true} and emits SyncComplete (member.rs:171-189). The rest arrives only after the next VvDigest round, 60 s later (election.rs:368, member.rs:207-213), and possibly after several rounds if the chain blocks again. History is eventually consistent, but the device reports synced and is eligible as successor too early.

confirmed.problem: The size cap acts on the provider's unverified size claim and makes the refusal permanent. After the first verified chunk, `attempt` reads `bf.size()` (download.rs:402-409), and `run` does the same through `known_size` for a partial blob (download.rs:318-321, 454-457). In iroh-blobs that value is the size header the provider sent; it is only checked once the last chunk arrives (`Bitfield::validated_size`). When the claim is over every requested cap, `check_size` returns `Admit::Refused`: the request turns `TooLarge`, `drop_tags` deletes the tags so garbage collection frees the partial data (download.rs:479-484), and `request()` keeps returning `TooLarge` (download.rs:232). The app then writes `app/refused/<hash>` (transfers.rs:593-598). From then on `cmd_download` answers TOO_LARGE (transfers.rs:654-656) and the fetch worker skips the hash (transfers.rs:163), across restarts, even when honest holders have it. BLAKE3 commits to the size only through the tree shape. So a holder of the real content can send a size header anywhere in the same power-of-two bucket: the root pair and the whole left subtree still verify.
confirmed.scenario: Alice posts a 20 MiB video (20480 chunks) in server S and goes offline. Mallory, a member, downloads it, then posts a message that references the same hash, which makes her an online author, tried before every other holder. Carol's auto-fetch connects to Mallory first. Mallory's modified provider sends the real tree but a size header of 30 MiB. 30720 chunks have the same 16384-chunk left subtree, so the root pair and the first chunk group verify. `check_size(30 MiB)` refuses, the transfer shows as failed, and Carol's store records `app/refused/<hash>`. Carol can never download the file again ("This file is larger than 25 MB"), although Bob holds it honestly. Every attachment between 16 MiB and 25 MiB is exposed, and every clip between 4 MiB and 5 MiB.
confirmed.fix: Refuse, and drop kinds, only on a validated size, proven by a last-chunk size proof. A provider that cannot prove its claim fails only its own attempt. (a) Add a pure `size_verdict(claimed: Option<u64>, validated: Option<u64>, have: u64, cap) -> {Ok, NeedProof, Refuse}`. It returns Refuse only when validated > cap or have > cap, and NeedProof when only the unvalidated claim is over the cap. Unit-test that an unvalidated claim over the cap never yields Refuse. (b) known_size() and the first-chunk check use bf.validated_size(); finish() already sees a complete, and so validated, size. (c) On NeedProof, abort the current stream and send execute_get(conn, GetRequest::blob_ranges(hash, ChunkRanges::last_chunk())) (iroh_blobs::protocol::ChunkRangesExt) to the same provider, then read validated_size(). Over the cap: Refused, which is correct and permanent because the hash commits to the length. Proof fails: Attempt::ProviderFailed for that provider only; mark it not pending and keep the request alive. Choose this over a plain ProviderFailed: swarm.rs:595-634 (oversized_downloads_are_refused) waits for TooLarge with total == size from an honest oversized provider and must keep passing. (d) Set d.total only from validated sizes (or keep the claim in a separate field). clips.rs:518 must then test only TooLarge or a validated total, or a fake claim on a merged clip and attachment request cancels the whole download. (e) Admit::Dropped/drop_tags follow the same rule. (f) Legacy app/refused/* rows were written from unvalidated claims. Move to a new key (for example app/refused2/<hash>, or store a validated flag) and ignore or delete the old rows at startup; a genuinely oversized blob is re-refused after one cheap proof. A test with a lying provider would need a hand-built response, so the pure-function test plus the existing swarm test are the minimum.
confirmed.verify: I could not refute any link in the chain. (1) iroh-blobs 0.105 fs store: import_bao_impl (store/fs.rs:1223) writes every batch with Bitfield::new_unchecked(ranges, size), where `size` is the response header (remote.rs:884). The only size check is `is_validated(size, leaf_range) && size != leaf_end`, and it fires only on the last chunk. Bitfield::size() is therefore the provider's claim; validated_size() (proto/bitfield.rs:132) is the trusted value. (2) execute_get(conn, local.missing()) asks for every range from chunk 0 up, so the last chunk comes last. (3) BLAKE3/bao: when the claimed and real chunk counts are in the same (2^k, 2^(k+1)] bucket, the root node is the same and its left subtree has the same shape. So the real root pair, the left-spine parents and leaf group 0 all verify. Progress(n>0) then reaches download.rs:400, observe().size() returns the claim, and check_size refuses. (4) Admit::Refused sets TooLarge, drop_tags runs, add_providers ignores TooLarge (download.rs:271), and request() repeats the refusal (232). transfers.rs:593-598 writes app/refused/<hash> for kind == Attachment. Nothing in the crate ever deletes that key. cmd_download (654) and the auto worker (163) honor it, so the refusal survives restarts and the UI cannot undo it. (5) Getting tried first is easy. providers() puts online authors first, Mallory can become one by reposting the hash, and the default auto_fetch_limit is 25 MiB, so Carol's client auto-fetches. Exposure: real attachments in (16 MiB, 25 MiB] (claim up to 32 MiB), and the Dropped path for merged requests. Clips are weaker: no app/refused row is written, and on_clip_transfer only cancels and forgets the pull, so it can be retried the next time the clip is heard. But clips.rs:518 also acts on `info.total > MAX_CLIP_BYTES`, and d.total is the same unvalidated claim (download.rs:406). A known_size()-based refusal also follows a restart after a partial fetch from Mallory. Major: any admitted member running a modified client can permanently stop a victim from downloading any attachment in that size range, and the victim has no recovery path.

confirmed.problem: Resuming a partial download whose hash has no references sends `who_has` to every conversation, and every answer counts as a nomination. Every clip pull falls in this branch, because clips get no `AttRef`. The `FetchReq::Resume` branch for `None` info (transfers.rs:197-212) does three things. It calls `who_has` for every server: the clip hash goes to every server's host. It adds every DM contact as a provider: DM `who_has` always returns the peer, so each contact, strangers included, is dialled and sees the hash. It calls `nominate(hash, conv, holders)` for all of them. When the download completes, `share_with_nominators` shares the blob with every conversation whose answer named the peer that delivered the last bytes. A host's answer is not checked, and hosting is not a privilege. So the host of an unrelated server can get the blob shared with, and announced to, its server.
confirmed.scenario: I start pulling a clip that P played in S1's voice room, and restart Tincan before the pull completes. On the first connection the resume asks every server. Mallory hosts S2, where P and I are also members. She learns the hash from the query and answers with P as a holder. P serves me, because the clip is shared with S1 and I am in S1. The pull completes with from = P. The nominations include (P, S2), so the clip is shared with S2 and announced to S2's host. Mallory then fetches the S1 clip from me, and every DM contact I have was dialled with its hash.
confirmed.fix: Stop fanning out and nominating in the no-reference branch. (1) Persist the pull's conversation: add `conv: Option<String>` to clips::Fetch with #[serde(default)]. Resume a Clip-kind partial through media: providers = the player (from fetch.by, address from the roster of fetch.conv) plus who_has(fetch.conv), with nominations for fetch.conv only, exactly like clip_fetch. A Clip partial with no Fetch record, or an old record with no conv: do not resume it, and drop its Clip tag (remove_kind) or leave it for GC. (2) An attachment partial with no references (lost index entry): do not resume it, or download only from providers that need no nomination and never call nominate(), so it stays unshared. (3) Factor the choice into a pure function, for example `resume_targets(kind, has_refs, fetch_conv: Option<ConvId>) -> Targets {Conv(c), RefConvs, None}`. Unit-test that a resumed clip asks only its own conversation and that no branch returns every conversation.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed. Clips never get an AttRef: share_blob and clip_fetch only share or nominate. Any unfinished clip pull keeps its Clip tag, because run() tags before the first byte, so partial_downloads lists it and the first on_connected sends FetchReq::Resume. att_info(...).filter(refs non-empty) is None, so the fan-out branch runs. It calls who_has in every net.convs() entry, adds every DM peer (net.rs:481 returns the peer with no network round trip), and nominate()s all of them. share_with_nominators on completion then shares the clip with every conversation that named `from`. finish_fetch puts the clip in the library, and announce() then sends it to every server in servers_sharing, S2 included. Scope corrections. (1) Holders are filtered: member.rs:217-222 keeps only current members of that server, so a hostile host can name any member of its own server, not anyone. P must also be in S2. (2) The S2 leg is a race: a session that is not yet Host or Member answers empty at once (session/mod.rs:568-580), and Resume fires on the first server connection. The DM leg is deterministic. (3) Providers are dialled one at a time until one completes (download.rs:335-366), so a DM contact sees the hash only when it comes before the provider that serves the clip. Pulls usually stay pending because the player went offline, so earlier providers often fail. Impact: the clip hash leaks to unrelated hosts and DM contacts (strangers' DM conversations included), and a clip already heard by everyone in the S1 voice room can be shared with S2. Low sensitivity, but it breaks the stated per-server compartmentalization. Requery does not do this, since the refs filter returns None for clips.

confirmed.problem: `open_with_default_app` runs `explorer.exe <path>` with `Command::arg`. Rust quotes an argument only when it contains a space or a tab. The Explorer command line uses commas as token separators: that is the `/select,<path>` syntax this file already works around with quotes in `reveal_arg`. `safe_file_name` keeps commas. So for an export path without spaces (the default `%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Tincan` usually has none), Explorer splits the path that `open_action` approved and does not open the file that was checked. Depending on which token Explorer acts on, it opens nothing or another file in the download folder.
confirmed.scenario: Honest case: someone sends `report,v2.pdf`. Open runs `explorer.exe C:\Users\me\Downloads\Tincan\report,v2.pdf`, which is tokenized at the comma, and the PDF does not open. Hostile case: a peer first sends `setup.exe` (Open reveals it, but the export stays in the folder), then `setup.exe,.pdf`. `open_action` sees a `.pdf` and returns Open. Explorer gets the unquoted `...\Tincan\setup.exe,.pdf`, and the first token names the executable exported earlier.
confirmed.fix: Lead with a pure argument builder: `pub(crate) fn open_arg(path: &Path) -> String { format!("\"{}\"", path.display()) }`, passed with raw_arg(open_arg(path)) (Windows paths cannot contain '"'). Unit-test it like reveal_selects_the_file, with C:\Users\me\Downloads\Tincan\report,v2.pdf (comma, no space) and a path with a space. Do not launch Explorer in tests. Correction to the proposed fix: windows-sys is NOT available to tincan-app. It is only in src-tauri/Cargo.toml, with features Win32_Foundation, Win32_Security, Win32_System_Threading and Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging, without Win32_UI_Shell. ShellExecuteExW (verb "open", lpFile = path) is the more robust option, but it adds a windows-sys dependency with Win32_UI_Shell to tincan-app (the crate is already in Cargo.lock). Defense in depth: map ',' to '_' in safe_file_name and update its tests. This is not enough alone, because the user-chosen download_dir can contain commas.
confirmed.verify: The code path is as described. open_with_default_app passes the exported path through Command::arg (shell.rs:290). Rust std on Windows quotes an argument only when it is empty or contains a space or tab (this follows std's append_arg as I know it; the toolchain has no rust-src to check against). explorer.exe is not a .bat or .cmd, so std does not force quotes. safe_file_name keeps ','. The default download_dir is %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Tincan (settings.rs:33-35), which has no space unless the user name has one. Explorer uses commas as token separators: reveal_arg already quotes for /select, and the comma behaviour is well known but I did not test it at runtime. So the honest case, an exported name such as report,v2.pdf in a space-free path, very likely fails to open the checked file. That is a real functional bug, and the open_action guarantee ('the file I checked is the file that opens') does not hold. The hostile case (setup.exe,.pdf launching the earlier setup.exe export) is unverified: it depends on which token Explorer acts on, which I could not establish. It is also softened. The earlier export of setup.exe got the Mark of the Web, written on every open_file before Reveal, so a launch would still show SmartScreen or the Attachment Manager warning naming setup.exe. '/' and ':' are replaced, so a peer cannot inject switches. Minor.

confirmed.problem: `HashInfo::share` keeps at most 16 conversations and evicts the oldest first (index.rs:91-93). The reshare rule in `index_attachments` (transfers.rs:295-301) adds a share whenever an author who may already fetch the blob references it, DM references included. A reference in a DM is posted by the DM peer, who already has access, so that share grants nothing. It does use a slot, and the slot it pushes out is the oldest share: usually the server the file was posted in, or the conversation I sent it to. `add_ref` evicts DM entries first for this reason; `share` does not.
confirmed.scenario: Alice sends a file to server S1; it is shared with S1. Mallory, a member of S1, mints invites (any member can) and brings 16 sybil identities into S1. Each sybil opens a DM with Alice and posts a message that references the hash. Each reference passes `allow_blob(sybil, hash)`, because the sybil is in S1, so `share(DM_i)` runs. After 16 of them, S1 is removed from the share list. `set_shared` drops it, Alice stops serving the file to S1 members and stops announcing it to S1's host. The sybils can then leave. Members who join later can't get the file from Alice, and the same works against every other holder.
confirmed.fix: (1) Skip the reshare for DM references: `let reshare = !dm && author != self.me && ...`. The only other party is the author, who already has access. This closes the eviction route. A complete blob gets no new nominations (cmd_download, auto-fetch and Peers all skip complete hashes, and request() for a held kind emits no Completed), so share_with_nominators cannot add DM shares after completion. (2) Defense in depth: have share() evict a DM share before a server share. That needs a per-entry dm flag in HashInfo.shared, persisted with #[serde(default)] in InfoRecord (for example `shared_dm: Vec<String>`, or objects with a default flag), with decode keeping old records readable. Pinning origin shares (sent or played there) is optional. (3) Tests: a pure `reshare_allowed(dm, author_is_me, complete, allowed) -> bool` unit test that a DM reference never reshares, and a HashInfo test where share(S1) followed by 16 DM shares leaves S1 shared. The existing shares_are_bounded test (oldest eviction among server shares) should still pass.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed after checking the limits that could have refuted it. (1) Any member can create invites: state.rs:631 accepts InviteCreate from any author. Admission is rate-limited, not capped: per creator a burst of 20 then 1 per minute, per invite a burst of 10 then 1 per 10 s (host.rs:50-57, 258-261). There is no member cap, so 16 sybils join in about a minute. (2) A sybil in S1 is a known peer, not a stranger. dm.rs accept_incoming calls open_conv for is_known_peer with no action from Alice, and each DM message reaches pump.rs:419 auto_fetch, then index_attachments (views.rs:395 also indexes on display). (3) In index_attachments, reshare is author != me && complete && allow_blob(sybil, hash), which is true because the sybil is in S1. `added | (reshare && i.share(conv))` uses the non-short-circuit '|', so share(DM_i) runs even when add_ref refuses the reference. (4) HashInfo::share removes index 0 past MAX_SHARED = 16, which is S1 (shared first by import_attachments). update_info then runs set_shared and announce: S1 members lose access through allow_blob, and the S1 host stops getting the Have. The DM shares remain after the sybils leave. Nothing restores S1 automatically: Alice's own references never reshare, and a new S1 member's repost fails allow_blob. Impact is availability only, per file and per holder, it needs 16 sybil identities, and S1 members who already have the file can still serve it to each other. Minor.

confirmed.problem: The new RosterSig early return also skips `rosters_changed`, so `requery_parked` no longer runs when a roster changes only in what the UI does not show. Addresses are one of those things. `requery_parked` is the one consumer that needs fresh addresses: `providers()` takes the provider's AddrHint from the roster (transfers.rs:481; clips.rs:505 does the same for clip pulls). `Files::add_providers` is the only thing that re-arms an already-failed provider (download.rs `merge` sets pending=true) and stores the new hint (`resolve` -> `lookup.add_endpoint_info`). Before this diff, every RosterUpdated ran that path, rate-limited to once per 10 s per hash.
confirmed.scenario: Bob downloads Alice's photo. Alice is online, but her roster hint is stale (her laptop moved networks, or her home relay URL arrived just after she connected). The 4 s dial fails, she is the only provider, and the request parks as Unavailable. The host then rebroadcasts the roster with Alice's new AddrHint. Her online state, voice, mute and share flags are unchanged, so RosterSig is equal and the pump returns at line 455: no rosters_changed, no requery_parked, no add_providers. Bob's card shows "no one online has it" while Alice is online. It stays that way until someone joins or leaves the server or Bob clicks Download. Before the diff, the rebroadcast re-armed Alice with her new address within 10 s.
confirmed.fix: Keep the UI skip but keep the re-arm. Store an address signature next to RosterSig in the same per-server entry, e.g. rosters: HashMap<ConvId, (RosterSig, Vec<(UserId, AddrHint)>)> with the (user, addr) pairs of roster.online sorted by user. The cleanups for lag, Left and connection changes then cannot drift apart. In the RosterUpdated arm: if only the address part changed, store it, set rosters_changed = true and call schedule(), with no mark() and no dms_dirty. Then return. A simpler choice that restores the old behaviour exactly is to set rosters_changed and schedule() on every RosterUpdated. That is still cheap: requery_parked only touches Unavailable hashes, throttles each to once per 10 s before queueing, and Requery adds only online providers (RESOURCES-2 stays fixed). Test it as a pure function, since Pump needs Core. For example, a fn roster_change(prev, &Roster) -> {ui: bool, requery: bool}: an RTT or revision change gives neither, an address-only change gives requery only, a mute gives both.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed against 806a3dc. Before that commit, every RosterUpdated set rosters_changed, so flush() ran requery_parked. That queued FetchReq::Requery (transfers.rs:177), which calls files.add_providers, and Download::merge sets pending=true and wakes the task. Now pump.rs:454-455 returns before line 460 when RosterSig is unchanged. RosterSig leaves out addresses, RTT and succession. The host does rebroadcast on an address-only change: host.rs:1719 marks the roster when p.remote != m.path.remote. Nothing else re-arms a provider that already failed. I checked every caller. start_download (Auto and Resume) skips a hash that already has a transfer. Only the user's Download click (transfers.rs:665), requery_on_new_ref, DmLinkUp, a lag and a roster change the UI can see reach Files::request or add_providers. A parked download (run loop: no pending provider, so Unavailable, then wake.notified()) stays parked while Alice is online. Three corrections to the scenario. (1) The address itself is not what is lost. Files is built on Net's endpoint (app.rs:163, endpoint.clone()), and note_roster calls learn_hint, which feeds Net's MemoryLookup (session/mod.rs:1514, inner.rs:283) on every roster. The dial would find the new address. The loss is only the re-arm. (2) A mute, voice or share change, DmLinkUp or a new reference also recovers it, not only a join or leave. (3) With Alice online, peers=1, so the card reads "1 person online has it" (Attachment.tsx:23), not "No one online has it". That claims a holder while nothing retries. The clips.rs:505 citation does not apply: Requery skips hashes with no att_info refs, so requery_parked never touches clip pulls. RESOURCES-9 was about UI refresh cost; skipping the requery is a side effect.

confirmed.problem: `lagged()` clears `self.conns`. The next ConnectionChanged for a Member server, which net also sends on mere RTT or path moves, therefore looks like a new connection, and line 472 calls `bulks.sync_started(server)`. No history sync is running, so no SyncComplete follows. `syncing` stays set until some window is cut at MAX_SYNC_BULK, and any open window's cap is stretched to started+60 s. The new APP-CORE-05 cap is meant to be 5 s outside a real sync; after a lag it is 60 s for every Member server.
confirmed.scenario: A large catch-up makes the pump's broadcast receiver lag, and lagged() clears conns. A second later each connected server sends an RTT-only ConnectionChanged(Member, same host). Every one of them is treated as a fresh connection and marked syncing, and no SyncComplete will clear it. Later one member of server S posts 50 messages a second. The rate opens a window with cap_len(S) = MAX_SYNC_BULK, so every live message in S, from everyone, is held for up to 60 s instead of being cut at 5 s. This repeats after every lag.
confirmed.fix: Remove self.conns.clear() from lagged(), or re-seed conns from self.core.net.connection(&conv) for each conv in net.convs(). Never call sync_started while re-seeding. rosters.clear(), Refresh::ALL and dms_dirty already cover what the clear was for. A sync the lag hid then gets the 5 s cap instead of 60 s, which is an acceptable cost. Optionally also drop syncing when a ConnectionChanged reports a state other than Member (add a Bulks::sync_ended), so a Member-to-Hosting move before SyncComplete cannot leave it set. Test: move the (state, host) tracking out of Pump into a small struct next to Bulks with on_change(server, state, host) -> (changed, start_sync) and on_lag(). Assert that after on_lag() an RTT-only change for (Member, same host) returns start_sync=false, and that a new host still returns true.
confirmed.verify: The mechanism holds. lagged() clears conns (pump.rs:354). publish_info sends ConnectionChanged on a material RTT move (25% and at least 10 ms) or a path change (session/mod.rs:1607-1621). The next such event for a Member server finds no entry, so insert() != Some(now) and sync_started runs (line 472). Nothing then sends SyncComplete: member.rs:181 sends it only once per Member role, when it first syncs. syncing is cleared only by sync_complete, by a cut at the cap in due() (line 201), or by forget. A window that ends on QUIET leaves it set. Three things limit the impact. (1) This is a hole in the new APP-CORE-05 cap, not a regression from before the diff: before 806a3dc a window had no maximum at all. (2) It costs one stretched window per Member server per lag, and only under a sustained flood: due() drops syncing at the 60 s cut, and then the capped rule applies. An ordinary burst still ends after QUIET, and a snapshot recovers held messages, so nothing is lost, only delayed. (3) A lag needs more than 4096 queued net events (EVENT_CAPACITY). A related hole the issue does not mention: if a lag drops a server's SyncComplete, or a server goes from Member to Hosting before SyncComplete, syncing stays set the same way. The proposed fix has its own hole: calling sync_started while re-seeding after a lag that hid both a reconnect and its SyncComplete sets syncing with nothing left to clear it.

confirmed.problem: `send` now empties the box and deletes `drafts[key]` when the send starts (setBox at line 80). If the Composer unmounts during the send, Shell.tsx keys ChannelChat/DmChat by channel or conv, so switching away is enough. A failure then writes the text back only to the module-level `drafts` map (line 93) and shows a toast. A Composer mounted for the same conversation in the meantime read `drafts` at mount, when it was empty, and never sees the restored text. Its next keystroke runs `change()` -> `drafts.set(key, v)` and overwrites the failed text. Before the diff the draft was kept until success, so this flow lost nothing.
confirmed.scenario: In #general, Alice writes a long message with an attachment and presses Enter. The import or host ack is slow. She clicks #random and back within a second. The new Composer for #general mounts empty, because drafts[#general] was deleted at send start. The send then fails ("Couldn't send this message."). The old instance is unmounted, so line 93 writes her text into drafts and a toast appears. Her box stays empty. She starts typing again, change() replaces drafts[#general], and the long message is gone. The attachment paths are dropped in this branch too (files: [] is written nowhere).
confirmed.fix: Send a failure to whichever Composer currently shows that key. Put the routing in lib/compose.ts as plain functions so the dependency-free pnpm test can reach it: a module-level Map<string, (sent: Draft) => void> with register(key, fn) returning an unregister function, and restoreFailed(key, sent, drafts) that calls the live handler when there is one and otherwise merges into drafts. In Composer, register (sent) => setBox(finishSend(box.current, sent, false)) in a useEffect on mount and unregister on unmount. In the !mounted.current branch call restoreFailed instead of drafts.set. Optionally keep files too (a draftFiles map read at mount), though that goes beyond restoring the old behaviour. Unit test: a failed send while another instance for the key is registered calls its handler with the sent text and files. With none registered, it lands in drafts in front of any typed text.
confirmed.verify: Confirmed against 842f990. Before it, send() left drafts[key] alone until success. A Composer that remounted for the same conversation during a send (Shell.tsx:35 and :54 key DmChat and ChannelChat, so switching remounts) read drafts at mount and showed the text. On failure the text stayed in the box. The error was silent: setError on an unmounted instance does nothing. Now setBox({text:'',files:[]}) at line 80 deletes drafts[key] when the send starts, so the new instance mounts empty. On a late failure, line 93 writes the text only into the module-level drafts map. The mounted instance never reads it again, and its next change() calls drafts.set(key, v), which overwrites it. If the user typed in the new box during the send, line 93 joins the two, but the next keystroke still drops the failed part. Late failures exist. sendMessage (store/actions.ts:648) awaits invoke and rejects. cmd_send_message can fail after a slow import_attachments, or when net.publish fails while waiting for the host's ack (commands.rs:231-240). The text survives only if the user switches away and back again before typing. Two notes on the issue: the toast is new (before, the failure was silent), and files are not a regression, since files were component state and were lost on any remount before the diff too. The diff also fixed the success case: before it, a remounted box showed text that had already been sent. That should be kept.

confirmed.problem: `VoiceParticipant.volume` was added to the contract (saved per-user volume, UI-LOGIC-13), but `Member` did not get it. VoiceRoomView therefore invents `volume: 1` for the tiles of a room you have not joined. Those tiles still open VolumePopover on right-click (Tile, `!isMe`). `initialVolume(undefined, p)` starts the slider at 100% over the saved value, and `onPointerUp`/`onKeyUp` sends `set_user_volume(user, v)` with it. The app saves this even outside voice (session.rs:793-804), and 1.0 deletes the saved entry.
confirmed.scenario: After a restart Alice has Jordan saved at 30%. She opens a voice room she has not joined and right-clicks Jordan's tile. The popover says 100%. Clicking the slider, or a keypress on it, without dragging sends set_user_volume(Jordan, 1.0), which removes the saved 30%. When she joins, Jordan plays at full volume.
confirmed.fix: Two pure changes in store/calls.ts, both testable with pnpm test. (1) Do not fake a known volume. Let preview tiles pass volume as unknown (undefined or null in the UI's own preview type) and hide the slider when it is unknown, for example with a showVolume(p) helper, so a preview tile's popover shows only the ID and Message. Alternatively, add the saved volume to the contract for members (Member.volume or a user_volumes command) and seed the slider from it. (2) In VolumePopover, send set_user_volume on pointer-up or key-up only if the value changed since the popover opened, for example with shouldSend(initial, current), which helps joined tiles too. Extend calls.test.ts: an unknown volume shows no slider, and an unchanged value sends nothing.
confirmed.verify: The bug is real but it is not a regression. The original code (git show 67b4fab:ui/src/components/VoiceView.tsx, line 17) started every popover at volumes.get(p.userId) ?? 1. Preview tiles were rendered with isMe={false} and opened the same popover, which sent onPointerUp and onKeyUp unconditionally. UI-LOGIC-13 (9424209) fixed joined tiles, which get VoiceParticipant.volume from the app, but left preview tiles unchanged with volume: 1 (line 261). The tracker's "fixed" for UI-LOGIC-13 is therefore only partly true. The harm is real: set_user_volume saves even outside voice, and 1.0 removes the saved entry (media/session.rs:799-804). Correction on the trigger: a click on the track moves the value, so the user sets what they see. Only a click on the thumb without moving it, or a key release that does not adjust the value, sends an unchanged 1.0. The keyup case is plausible because Popover focuses the first input on open (Menu.tsx:59), which is the slider, so releasing Space, Enter or Shift there sends 1.0. Moving the slider from a displayed 100% also overwrites the saved 30% with a value the user chose from a false starting point.
